note: Canonical terminology registry. A term is preferred (the wording Prumo uses), deprecated (outgoing wording, must name its replacement) or forbidden (must not appear in current documentation). Matching is whole-word and case-insensitive.

terms.definition: The single declared unit of intent a run is authorized to pursue. A Goal carries acceptance criteria and is locked before implementation begins.
A stable-identity, provider-neutral record of knowledge (requirement, decision, evidence, fact) that the workforce reads and writes.
A derived, non-canonical pack of the smallest sufficient context for one Goal, produced by the context compiler.
A generated projection of the instruction IR into a vendor-specific instruction file (AGENTS.md, .cursor rules, skills). Never canonical.
Owning project truth. A canonical document is the source other surfaces resolve to.
A derived surface that must resolve back to a canonical source; it never owns facts.
A planned, verifiable increment of implementation with explicit exit criteria (see docs/development/waves.md).
A document kept in sync with the code it describes, with drift treated as a defect.
Retired wording for the role that validates a surface before it is trusted.
A declared, deterministic check that produces evidence which must pass before a run may claim success.
Forbidden: it names a technique as the product's identity, which misstates what Prumo is. Describe the mechanism instead (context compilation, instruction IR).
